sovereign_country.strategic_role: 苏伊士运河经济特区、辐射中东及北非的低成本轻工制造

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Wholesale Importation of Deep-Frozen Meat Carcasses and Pelagic Fish

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (with Islamic Sharia as the principal source of legislation per Article 2 of the Egyptian Constitution of 2014)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Egypt-United Kingdom Agreement for the Encouragement and Protection of Investments (1976, active)
Egypt-United States Treaty Concerning the Encouragement and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (1986, entered into force 1992)
Greater Arab Free Trade Area (GAFTA) Agreement (1997)
Agadir Agreement for the Establishment of a Free Trade Zone among the Arab Mediterranean Nations (2004)
Treaty of the Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa (COMESA) (Egypt acceded 1998)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 80 of 2002 on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing, as amended by Law No. 36 of 2014 and Law No. 144 of 2019; Executive Regulations of Law 80/2002 issued by Prime Ministerial Decree No. 631 of 2015, as amended; Investment Law No. 72 of 2017, Article 91 and its Executive Regulations (mandating beneficial ownership disclosure to the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones - GAFI); Companies Law No. 159 of 1981, as amended; Central Bank of Egypt AML/CFT Regulations and the Egyptian Financial Regulatory Authority's AML directives.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Good Standing of the non-Egyptian corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry in the shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (if shareholder state is a Convention party) OR Consular Legalization at the Egyptian Embassy or Consulate in that state

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution authorizing incorporation of the Egyptian LLC and appointing its representatives
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the foreign parent company

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Memorandum and Articles of Association of the non-Egyptian shareholder (certified true copy)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry in the shareholder's country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney in favour of the Egyptian establishment lawyer or local nominee shareholder
AML/KYC bank reference letter for the foreign shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Correspondent bank of the foreign shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus Hague Apostille (if the bank is in an apostille state) OR Consular Legalization

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against UN Security Council Consolidated Lists, EU consolidated sanctions lists, U.S. OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List, the Central Bank of Egypt Sanctions List, and the Egyptian AML Watch Lists. Enhanced due diligence is required for any PEP owning more than 10% of the LLC or occupying senior management positions. Screens must be performed at onboarding, at incorporation, and monthly throughout the first operational year; all results must be retained for 5 years per AML Law No. 80/2002.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: GAFI Investor Services Portal (gafi.gov.eg) and the Egyptian Electronic Commercial Registry System
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be registered in Arabic script. A common-law English transliteration is permitted for foreign correspondence but the Arabic name is the legal identity. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to a pre-registered name or protected trademark. Names must be grammatically sound in Arabic and must not contain non-transliterable or offensive terms.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If GAFI rejects a proposed name, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal with the GAFI Legal Affairs Department within 15 business days of notification. The appeal must contain a fresh name search report and a corrected name. GAFI is required to decide within 10 business days. If the administrative appeal is denied, the applicant may either file a new name reservation application or initiate judicial review before the Administrative Court (Court of First Instance) under Law No. 106 of 2013 on Administrative Judiciary. A name reservation is extendable once for an additional 30 days upon payment of the standard renewal fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office addresses are not accepted for the LLC incorporation certificate or the commercial registry listing; a physical, dedicated commercial office is required under Articles 44-46 of Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 and GAFI registration guidelines. For cold-chain meat and seafood import operations, the registered office must host at least one employee with health clearance and retain physical or permanent digital records of import permits, customs declarations, and food safety certifications.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 45% probability of an unannounced physical inspection within the first 12 months of operation, attributable to joint inspections by the Egyptian Food Safety Authority (GFSHA) and the General Organization for Export and Import Control (GOEIC) under Food Safety Law No. 92 of 2016 and Decree No. 589 of 2020.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: GAFI name reservation and company incorporation administrative fees (Fast Track application)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: GAFI Service Tariffs 2024; Government Service Fee Schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: National Company Registry electronic filing and commercial registration stamp fees
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Trade and Industry / Egyptian Commercial Registry
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Commercial Registry Law No. 34 of 1976 fee table

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and apostillation / consular legalization of five foreign corporate documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs Consular Department and/or designated apostille authority in the origin country
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Consular Tariff Schedule MFAA 2024; apostille flat fees in the competent origin authority

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified Arabic translation and Arabisation of the Memorandum and Power of Attorney (approximately 40 pages)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Accredited sworn translation office recognized by GAFI and the Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated translator tariff; GAFI language compliance requirement

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Egyptian legal counsel for pre-incorporation due diligence, drafting of incorporation contract and POA, and representation before GAFI
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing international law firm benchmark for Egypt; engagement-based fee (20-40 hours)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office commercial address and ancillary rent deposit for first year (25 sq m office in Alexandria or Cairo trade district)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark commercial lease rate for a 25 sq m office in a designated commercial area

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Food import pre-licensing consultation and GFSHA/GOEIC license filing fee (preliminary veterinary and food safety clearances for ISIC 4632)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Egyptian Food Safety Authority (GFSHA) / General Organization for Export and Import Control (GOEIC)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Implementing decree tariff under Food Safety Law No. 92 of 2016

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Bank account opening and AML/KYC fee for the LLC (incl. foreign entity registration with the national bank and CBE)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Commercial bank in Egypt (e.g., NBE, Banque Misr)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank service tariff for LLC accounts; prevailing market practice

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Companies Law No. 159 of 1981, as amended by Law No. 4 of 2009, Articles 201 et seq. governing Limited Liability Companies; Investment Law No. 72 of 2017, Articles 10-12 and its Executive Regulations regarding GAFI one-stop incorporation; Import Registration Law No. 121 of 1982, as amended, together with Executive Decree No. 43 of 2016, as amended by Decree No. 991 of 2022.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI), One-Stop Shop for Company Formation and Commercial Registry Services; the Commercial Registry Office under the Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade acting through GAFI.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association (Arabic: Aqd Al-Taasis wal-Nizam Al-Asasi) authenticated before the Notary Public and filed with GAFI for the issuance of the Commercial Register Excerpt.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to LLC formation under Law No. 159 of 1981; the founders freely fix the capital, which must be fully subscribed and deposited into a temporary escrow account at a licensed Egyptian bank before GAFI registration, evidenced by an official capital deposit certificate. However, to qualify as a registered importer of frozen meat and seafood under GOEIC rules, the LLC must maintain paid-up capital of no less than EGP 5,000,000 (approximately USD 103,000) and provide proof of financial solvency.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) The paid-up share capital of the Limited Liability Company, fully subscribed and deposited in escrow account No. [●] at [Bank], is ratified in accordance with Egyptian Companies Law No. 159 of 1981, including any in-kind contributions valued by the appointed expert. (2) The registered office is established at [address], Cairo, Egypt, and the lease for those premises is ratified as the legal seat for commercial registry, tax and administrative purposes. (3) [Name] is appointed Manager with sole signing authority, and [Name] is appointed co-signatory for bank matters. (4) The officers are authorised to file all incorporation forms, pay fees, and complete registrations with GAFI, the Tax Authority, Social Insurance and GOEIC.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve the LLC Trade Name and Verify Activity Eligibility
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI E-Services Portal / GAFI Investor Services Center, Cairo
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File an electronic name reservation application on the GAFI investor portal selecting the Limited Liability Company form, provide three alternative names in Arabic and/or English, describe the intended activity as import and wholesale of frozen beef and seafood, and pay the online reservation fee. GAFI reserves the approved name for 60 days, after which the reservation lapses if not used.
required_dossiers: Passport copies or national ID copies of each founding partner
Completed name reservation application form
List of three alternative trade names
Description of intended business scope (ISIC 4632 frozen meat and seafood import)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for similarity, religious sensitivity, or inconsistency with public order, file a revised application within 7 business days; an internal appeal may be submitted to the GAFI Legal Department against an unjustified refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Authenticate the Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Justice – Notary Public Office; alternatively the GAFI Notary Desk at the One-Stop Shop
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Arabic incorporation contract stating the firm name, registered office, object, capital, quota allocation, and manager appointment provisions. All partners or their legal representatives must appear in person before the Notary Public to attest identity and capacity, sign the contract, and pay notary stamp taxes. The notarized original is then used as the controlling instrument for GAFI filing.
required_dossiers: Draft Memorandum and Articles of Association in Arabic
Passport or national ID of every shareholder and signatory
GAFI name reservation certificate
Power of attorney executed and legalized abroad, if signing by proxy
Notarized or legalized lease documentation for the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Notarial observations are cured by amending the disputed clause and re-authenticating the contract; foreign-issued documents must be legalized by the Egyptian consulate and translated into Arabic by a certified translator before re-presentation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Capital Escrow Account and Obtain Deposit Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Egyptian commercial bank with a one-stop corporate formation desk, e.g. National Bank of Egypt or Banque Misr
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the authenticated incorporation contract and name reservation certificate to the bank, complete the corporate account opening and anti-money-laundering (AML) due diligence forms, and transfer the subscribed paid-up capital into a temporary escrow account. The bank issues an official capital deposit certificate and a no-objection letter addressed to GAFI confirming that the capital is blocked until commercial registration is completed.
required_dossiers: Authenticated Articles of Association
GAFI name reservation certificate
Partners' identification and proof of source of funds
Bank account opening forms and beneficial ownership declaration
AML/KYC questionnaire completed for each ultimate shareholder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank raises KYC or beneficial-ownership queries, supply supplementary notarized declarations and source-of-wealth evidence; if the account is refused, the founders may select another licensed bank without restarting the GAFI procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit Incorporation Dossier to GAFI and Obtain Commercial Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop, Companies Registration Department, Cairo
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Deliver the notarized incorporation contract, bank capital deposit certificate, registered office lease, manager appointment form, and specimen signatures to GAFI. Pay the registration fee, notarization fee, and stamp duties; upon legal review, GAFI records the company in the Commercial Registry and issues the Commercial Register Excerpt and the Company Statistical Card (increment number). Publish the incorporation summary in the official gazette if required by law.
required_dossiers: Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association
Bank capital deposit certificate
Registered office lease or ownership deed
Manager appointment form and acceptance declaration
Passport copies of the first manager and directors
GAFI fee payment receipts
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI issues a deficiency memorandum, rectify the specified clauses and resubmit within 10 business days; a full refusal may be appealed to the GAFI Chairman within 30 days and thereafter to the administrative judiciary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register with the Tax Authority and Social Insurance Authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) regional tax office; National Organization for Social Insurance (NOSI)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the Commercial Register Excerpt and Statistical Card, file the electronic registration at the ETA office to obtain the unified Tax Identification Number and the tax card. Register the LLC for payroll withholding, VAT, and stamp tax obligations. Simultaneously open the employer file at NOSI for future Egyptian workforce enrollment and obtain the social insurance registration number.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register Excerpt
Company Statistical Card
Tax card application forms
Manager's national ID and specimen signature
Registered office lease and utility bill
Board resolution appointing officers and bank signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the ETA or NOSI defers registration for incomplete foreign documents, provide certified Arabic translations and legalized powers of attorney; an administrative appeal may be lodged with the head of the relevant registration sector within 15 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register as an Importer in the GOEIC Importers Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Organization for Export and Import Control (GOEIC), Importer Registration Department, Cairo
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the importer registration dossier establishing Egyptian legal personality, import activity scope, paid-up capital of at least EGP 5,000,000, and appointment of a responsible import officer. Upon approval, GOEIC issues the Importer Registration Certificate, which must be presented to Egyptian Customs for each consignment of frozen meat and seafood. Maintain the GOEIC annual compliance file and update any changes in the company's legal form or officer appointments.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register Excerpt showing 'Importation and Wholesale of Frozen Foods'
Income tax card and VAT registration certificate
Bank capital certificate or audited financial statements evidencing paid-up capital
Importer registration application form
Board resolution appointing the responsible import officer
Company seal and signature specimens
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, correct the commercial register activity description or capital evidence and resubmit; a formal rejection may be appealed to the GOEIC Registration Committee within 30 days and subsequently to the administrative court.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: National Food Safety Authority (NFSA) for food facility licensing and import conformity; General Organization for Export and Import Control (GOEIC) for customs import clearance; Industrial Development Authority (IDA) if a purpose-built cold storage industrial installation is constructed.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Food Facility Operating License for Cold Storage and Wholesale Distribution of Frozen Meat, Poultry and Seafood, issued by the NFSA; each consignment additionally requires a Veterinary Quarantine Permit from the General Organization for Veterinary Services (GOVS).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA), Ministry of Environment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B – Environmental Impact Assessment Screening under Law No. 4 of 1994 as amended by Law No. 9 of 2009 and Ministerial Decree No. 964 of 2015; a full EIA Report (Category C) is triggered if ammonia refrigeration charge exceeds the regulatory threshold or the facility treats and disposes of process wastewater on-site.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Cold storage facilities must discharge no untreated process effluents; defrost condensate and cleaning wastewater routed to the public sewer must comply with the limits of Law No. 48 of 1982 and the standards of the competent governorate water utility (e.g., BOD ≤ 400 mg/L, COD ≤ 600 mg/L, TSS ≤ 400 mg/L, oil and grease ≤ 100 mg/L). Refrigerant gas management must comply with Law No. 38 of 2002 on ozone-depleting substances; spoiled meat and seafood waste must be disposed of through licensed landfill or rendering facilities under Ministry of Environment waste management rules.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety and civil defense clearance certificate from the General Administration of Civil Defense of the Ministry of Interior for the cold store; structural load inspection and building safety approval from the local governorate engineering administration for the refrigeration plant and ammonia machine room; and occupational safety and health workplace clearance from the Ministry of Manpower confirming compliance with temperature, ventilation, and worker protection standards for cold-environment operations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), Ministry of Finance – official portal: https://eta.gov.eg / https://www.invoice.eta.gov.eg (e-invoicing)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity must obtain a Tax Card and Tax Identification Number (TIN) from the local tax office (Ciniplex) for the jurisdiction in which its registered branch or representative office is located; submit the company commercial registration, lease/deed for business premises, power of attorney, and passport copy of the legal representative; the ETA issues the Tax Card after a physical inspection; a separate VAT ID is obtained through the VAT registration module on the ETA portal (TIN is used as VAT ID upon registration).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; resident LLC taxed on worldwide income; non-resident branch taxed on Egypt-source income only
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No general check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election under Egyptian law; entity classification is fixed under the Companies Law and Income Tax Law; foreign investors may elect treaty-consistent permanent establishment treatment where a DTA applies; special economic zone projects may elect an alternative tax concessions regime under the SEZ Law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT under Law No. 67/2016 as amended)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 annual taxable turnover; exporters and importers may be required to register regardless of threshold when claiming zero-rating or carrying on taxable activity
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: ETA mandates e-invoicing and e-receipts through the national electronic invoice portal. Taxpayers above turnover thresholds (phased per ETA decisions) must integrate APIs for real-time submission and XML/JSON validation. A unique invoice code (UUID and QR code) is issued by the ETA after automated clearance; clearance is near-real-time with pre-issuance validation for large taxpayers, and stamping/QR codes are mandatory on printed copies.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rated for exported goods physically leaving Egypt under a customs export declaration; zero-rated for services supplied to a non-resident and consumed outside Egypt, subject to documentary evidence. The exporter must be VAT-registered and issue a valid e-invoice reflecting zero-rate; goods must be shipped within the period prescribed by the Customs Law; services must be connected to a real overseas contract and utilized abroad.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (declaration no. and date, customs release certificate)
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill evidencing actual shipment from Egypt to foreign buyer
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) confirming foreign currency proceeds credited to the Egyptian exporter’s bank account through an authorized bank
Commercial invoice issued under e-invoicing rules
Purchase orders/international sales contract and, where applicable, certificate of origin
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ETA and Customs Authority jointly audit export consignment files; failure to substantiate physical export or remittance within the 180-day repatriation window triggers reversal of zero-rating with VAT at 14%, plus late payment interest charged at the Central Bank lending rate plus 2% per month or fraction thereof; fraudulent claims carry penalties of up to double the tax due and imprisonment under VAT Law Article 44, Customs Law smuggling penalties, and administrative stop on the exporter's e-invoicing profile.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) - General Administration of Foreign Exchange; banking supervision is exercised through the CBE Banking Control Sector, with capital-account coordination delegated to the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt operates a de facto current-account convertibility regime for trade, freight, insurance and after-tax profit remittances; licensed banks may execute import payments and profit transfers without individual CBE pre-approval provided the underlying documents are complete. Capital-account transactions remain subject to enhanced validation under Law No. 194 of 2020 on the Central Bank and Banking System and through GAFI registration. The EGP is not freely convertible on capital account: foreign capital contributions, liquidation proceeds and cross-currency swaps require the bank to file a capital-entry or capital-repatriation reference with the CBE and GAFI. Profit remittance hurdles are primarily documentary: the Egyptian bank must hold audited financial statements, a valid tax card, proof of dividend withholding tax settlement, and evidence that the EGP equivalent was purchased at the bank's dealing-room rate with no parallel-market source. Since the 2024 exchange-rate liberalisation, the CBE no longer publishes a fixed official rate, but temporary FX scarcity may still create bank-level rationing and postponement of discretionary remittances.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: The CBE's export-proceeds rules require all export receipts to be repatriated to Egypt through a licensed Egyptian bank and credited to the exporter's foreign-currency account. The standard statutory collection timeline is the invoice tenor or the maturity of the export letter of credit, with a maximum banking-period limit normally not exceeding 180 days from the date of the bill of lading; after that period the bank must escalate the position to the CBE and the exporter must transfer the proceeds immediately. The mandatory conversion ratio is currently nil because Egypt maintains a unified, market-determined exchange rate; exporters may keep 100% of the proceeds in foreign currency. However, the CBE retains statutory power under exceptional FX-control instructions to impose a temporary surrender ratio; in such a declaration, exporters may be required to convert 100% of new export receipts into EGP within the period fixed by the CBE circular.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Egypt does not recognise offshore digital EMI platforms as receiving banks for import settlements, EGP clearing, or CBE foreign-trade reporting. Only CBE-licensed banks and registered payment-service providers under Law No. 194 of 2020 can hold settlement accounts and route SWIFT MT103 or letter-of-credit messages. An offshore digital EMI may be used only as an ancillary visibility tool or virtual-card issuer for treasury expenses; it cannot replace the licensed banking channel for the LLC's frozen-beef and seafood import disbursements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Mandatory physical presence applies to the LLC's manager, all authorised signatories and all ultimate beneficial owners holding more than 25% of the share capital. Remote account opening is not permitted for a newly incorporated foreign-owned Egyptian entity. The bank requires a face-to-face interview at its branch in Egypt, original passports, an apostilled or consular-legalised board resolution, and original Arabic-language constitutional documents. If a manager cannot travel, the bank may accept a notarised power of attorney to a local resident, but the UBO must complete a video-call compliance interview and, for state-owned banks, appear physically within the bank's specified grace period.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore UBO opacity or incomplete GAFI/commercial registration package
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified Arabic translation of the LLC constitutional documents; GAFI incorporation certificate; commercial register extract; tax registration card; ultimate-ownership chart drawn to natural persons; board resolution naming signatories; passport copies and residence history of UBOs; bank-neutral source-of-funds statement for each foreign shareholder.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering indicators: dual invoicing, undervaluation of frozen meat cargo, customs valuation mismatch
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised commercial proforma invoice; independent pre-shipment inspection certificate covering weight, temperature, quantity and packaging; customs ACI/ACID declaration; bill of lading; export quotation cross-referenced to international meat price indices; importer's pricing declaration under the General Organization for Export and Import Control (GOEIC) rules.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions exposure or high-risk correspondent routing through intermediary accounts in the UAE, Turkey or Hong Kong
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full ownership and beneficial-ownership chart of the seller; compliance declaration confirming no UN/EU/US/UK sanctions nexus; direct bank-to-bank SWIFT chain without shell intermediaries; vessel AIS and charter-party evidence unless an original bill of lading is supplied; bank confirmation representing the ultimate correspondent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Frozen beef or seafood blocked-origin or veterinary/customs refusal risk
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Country-of-origin certificate; valid import permit issued through GOEIC; veterinary health certificate and quarantine clearance from the General Organization for Veterinary Services; halal certification for beef; Ministry of Health or military-quarantine clearance; laboratory residue certificate where the commodity schedule requires it.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The initial equity injection must be routed by SWIFT MT103 or MT202 cover payment from the shareholder's corporate bank to the LLC's foreign-currency account at a CBE-licensed Egyptian bank. The remittance instruction must specify the LLC legal name in Arabic and English, the GAFI investment-file number, the receiving bank SWIFT BIC, and the narrative 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION - GAFI FILE Reference - EG_LLC'. The bank will code the transaction in the CBE balance-of-payments reporting framework as an inward foreign direct investment contribution, will place the funds in a capital escrow sub-account, and will notify GAFI. After the bank matches the GAFI capital certificate and the LLP's commercial registration, the funds are released to the operational account. The manager must not convert the foreign currency into EGP until the LLC holds a valid tax card and the GAFI quarterly investment report has been updated.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Permitted clearing rails for trade settlement are: (i) an irrevocable commercial letter of credit opened by a tier-1 Egyptian bank and issued by SWIFT MT700, settled by MT103/MT754/MT742 at sight or 90-day tenor; (ii) open-account SWIFT MT103 supplier payments after import customs clearance, supported by the ACI number and bank-approved import invoice; and (iii) documentary collections under URC 522 for fast-turnaround seafood consignments. All outbound disbursements require the customs ACI/ACID reference, GOEIC import permit, VAT and tax registration cards, signed proforma invoice, ocean or air bill of lading, insurance certificate, and veterinary/health clearance for the specific cargo. Repayments to foreign shareholders must be classified as profit remittance and supported by audited financial statements and tax-clearance evidence, and cannot be executed before the CBE bank validation checks are completed.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain vanilla deliverable FX forwards in EGP/USD or EGP/EUR between the LLC and a licensed Egyptian bank, for the tenor of an underlying import LC or trade payable
Cross-currency swaps (CCS) between USD and EGP offered by resident banks for matched import and export cash-flow conversion, subject to CBE capital-account reporting

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) permitted offshore for non-resident counterparties hedging EGP exposure; the resident EG LLC may enter an NDF only through a bank-approved hedging line evidencing genuine underlying trade exposure

FX options and exotic derivatives are not generally permissible; they require bank pre-clearance and, if offered at all, must be documented as a genuine trade hedge for frozen meat and seafood imports
Package trade hedge consisting of LC discounting or supplier delayed-payment terms combined with a roll-over FX forward to cover repayment currency risk

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual audited financial statements deposition with the Commercial Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: GAFI Commercial Registry (General Authority for Investment and Free Zones)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the fiscal year-end stated in the LLC's articles (Egyptian tax default year is 30 June, unless a calendar-year election is made under Law No. 91/2005)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of EGP 1,000-5,000 (approximately USD 20-100 per current exchange rate); commercial registration flag becomes non-compliant; continuous default exceeding 12 months invokes administrative strike-off and dissolution proceedings under Companies Law No. 159/1981.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (Form No. 2)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months after the end of the fiscal year (31 October for a 30 June fiscal year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly additional tax equal to 2% of the tax due computed retroactively from the filing deadline, plus an administrative fine of EGP 200-500 per month of delay; persistent default leads to tax collection orders, asset attachment, and customs/clearance restrictions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial ownership (UBO) register update and confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after each annual general assembly that approves the annual financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine of up to EGP 100,000 (approximately USD 3,000) under the anti-money laundering framework; trade license suspension, dividend distribution prohibitions, and referral to the Egyptian Economic Prosecution for intentional non-disclosure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual trade license renewal and commercial register maintenance certificate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Governorate Trade Licensing Department and GAFI One-Stop Shop
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Each calendar year on or before the expiry date of the issued trade license (typically 31 December)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Daily surcharge until renewal and potential sealing/seizure of import cold-storage premises; two consecutive years of non-renewal results in deregistration, commercial register strike-off, and loss of the import license.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No size or turnover exemption applies to LLCs incorporated in Egypt: every LLC must appoint at least one accredited Egyptian auditor and present audited financial statements to the annual general assembly; audited accounts are also mandatory for the renewal of the commercial registration and frozen-food import license.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS) issued by the Ministry of Finance under Decree No. 110 of 2015, substantially converged with IFRS; full IFRS is accepted for listed and Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA) regulated entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The LLC must maintain a Beneficial Ownership Register identifying every natural-person ultimate beneficial owner holding at least 25% of shares, voting rights, or control; any change is filed with GAFI within 30 days, and an annual confirmation is submitted at the AGM along with the approved annual financial statements.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Commercial Registry Extract and Current Trade License
Statutory ledger ledger of LLC contributions/distributions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600 - 2,200 per annum (GAFI-licensed registered office and resident agent in Cairo or Alexandria)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 900 - 4,000 per annum depending on transaction volume, inventory count scope, and LC confirmation work required by the frozen beef and seafood import business

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 22.5% corporate income tax on taxable profits of Egyptian resident companies and Egyptian-source profits of non-residents
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general reduced corporate income tax rate applies to an ordinary Egyptian LLC conducting frozen meat and seafood importation. Statutory incentives may apply only where the entity qualifies under a specific investment, free-zone, economic-zone, or sectoral incentive regime. Tax holidays are not generally available to ordinary mainland importers. Taxable income is computed from accounting profit with statutory adjustments, including deductible-expense, depreciation, bad-debt, interest-limitation, and documentation requirements.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual corporate income tax return for legal persons, commonly identified by the Egyptian Tax Authority as Form 29 or its successor electronic legal-person return, filed through the Egyptian Tax Authority electronic tax return portal. The precise form version and portal workflow should be confirmed against the taxpayer's current ETA registration and filing profile.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual. Corporate income tax is generally declared through one annual return; periodic tax obligations may separately arise for VAT, payroll withholding, professional withholding, stamp tax, and other taxes.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return is generally due within four months after the end of the financial year. For a calendar-year taxpayer, the ordinary deadline is 30 April of the following year. The return and financial statements must be electronically submitted where the taxpayer is within the mandatory electronic-filing population.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, legal form, commercial registration number, tax registration number, unified tax file information, registered address, activity code, branch details, contact information, and authorized signatory.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident must report the Egyptian permanent establishment, branch, project, or other taxable presence, use the Egyptian tax registration details, and identify only Egyptian-source or Egyptian-permanent-establishment income within the applicable filing scope.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Accounting period and return status section
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Financial year start and end dates, first return, amended return, cessation return, liquidation status, and applicable accounting basis.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the accounting period attributable to the Egyptian taxable presence. A non-resident without a taxable presence should generally not file a full resident-company return solely because it receives treaty-protected income, unless required by the ETA or an Egyptian withholding, assessment, or registration obligation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit or loss shown in the approved financial statements before Egyptian corporate income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a branch or permanent establishment, start with the accounts attributable to Egyptian activities and apply consistent allocation of assets, functions, risks, expenses, and financing in accordance with Egyptian law and the arm's-length principle.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Taxable revenue and other income section
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Sales, trading income, service income, foreign-exchange gains, finance income, gains on disposal, recoveries, and other taxable receipts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include Egyptian-source income and income attributable to the Egyptian permanent establishment. Import purchases are not income; subsequent gross-margin revenue from Egyptian sales must be recognized under the applicable accounting and tax rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Cost of goods sold and deductible operating expenses section
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Opening and closing inventory, imported purchase cost, freight, insurance, customs-related costs, cold-chain costs, warehousing, payroll, rent, utilities, repairs, and documented business expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses must be incurred for the business, supported by legally acceptable documents, and appropriately allocated to Egyptian activities. Import customs documentation, bills of lading, supplier invoices, payment records, and inventory records should reconcile to the return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Tax depreciation and capital allowances section
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax depreciation for qualifying fixed assets, including refrigeration equipment, cold-storage infrastructure, vehicles, warehouse equipment, and information systems, with accounting-to-tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident may claim only depreciation properly attributable to the Egyptian taxable presence and supported by ownership, capitalization, use, and asset-register evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-back of non-business expenses, unsupported expenses, prohibited payments, certain provisions, penalties, income tax, and expenses subject to statutory limitations or documentation failures.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not deduct head-office or related-party charges without demonstrable benefit, allocation methodology, contractual support, arm's-length evidence, and proof of actual performance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Purchases, sales, services, financing, guarantees, royalties, management charges, imports, and other dealings with related parties, together with pricing adjustments and required transfer-pricing disclosures.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose Egyptian related-party dealings and maintain local-file, master-file, and country-by-country reporting documentation where applicable. Customs valuation and transfer-pricing positions must be reconciled or technically explained.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Tax losses and carried-forward losses section
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Current-year tax loss, utilized prior-year losses, remaining carried-forward losses, and statutory five-year utilization period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use losses only to the extent attributable to the same Egyptian taxable taxpayer or permanent establishment and supported by filed returns and underlying records. Egypt generally does not provide a general corporate tax loss carryback.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Taxable profit and corporate income tax computation section
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Adjusted taxable profit, allowable loss utilization, taxable base, 22.5% corporate income tax calculation, prior payments, credits, and balance payable or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the ordinary 22.5% rate unless a documented statutory incentive or treaty rule affects the computation. Treaty relief normally does not eliminate Egyptian tax on profits attributable to an Egyptian permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Advance payments, creditable withholding taxes, tax payments, prior assessments, payment references, and reconciliation to the general ledger and tax account.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only withholding credits supported by Egyptian withholding certificates or other ETA-accepted evidence. Reconcile tax withheld from suppliers, employees, lenders, licensors, and non-resident service providers.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Financial statements, schedules, and certification attachments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Approved financial statements, trial balance, tax reconciliation, depreciation schedule, inventory schedule, related-party schedules, withholding reconciliations, and transfer-pricing documents where required.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach or retain the Egyptian-permanent-establishment accounts, attribution workpapers, intercompany agreements, allocation keys, and evidence supporting cross-border deductions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer declaration, authorized representative details, electronic signature or authenticated filing credentials, date of submission, and payment reference.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The authorized Egyptian representative must have valid filing authority and preserve the electronic submission receipt, acknowledgment, payment confirmation, and any ETA correspondence.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing, non-filing, inaccurate filing, failure to maintain records, and failure to provide information may trigger penalties under the Unified Tax Procedures Law No. 206 of 2020 and related regulations. Penalties depend on the violation and repetition; late or non-submission penalties may range from approximately EGP 3,000 to EGP 50,000 for initial violations and from approximately EGP 50,000 to EGP 2,000,000 for repeated or aggravated violations. Tax remains payable, and interest or additional amounts may accrue on unpaid tax. Deliberate concealment, false invoices, fraudulent books, or tax evasion may create criminal exposure in addition to administrative penalties.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Generally 10% Egyptian withholding tax on dividends distributed by an Egyptian company to a non-resident shareholder, subject to domestic exemptions, listed-company rules, participation conditions, and applicable double-tax treaty relief. A 5% domestic rate may apply in specified qualifying participation or listed-share circumstances; eligibility must be tested against the relevant statutory conditions and current ETA practice.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The Egyptian payer should obtain and retain a valid certificate of tax residence from the recipient, verify beneficial ownership and treaty entitlement, confirm any minimum ownership, holding-period, limitation-on-benefits, or anti-abuse conditions, and apply the treaty rate only where the procedural requirements are satisfied. The payer should document the payment, recipient identity, ownership chain, board or shareholder approval, withholding computation, remittance, and withholding certificate. Where advance approval, refund, or treaty-clearance procedures are required, the recipient or payer should submit the treaty claim and residence certificate to the ETA before or promptly after payment in accordance with current administrative practice. Treaty relief is not available merely because the recipient is incorporated in a treaty country.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Egyptian domestic withholding tax is generally 20% on royalties and interest paid to non-residents where the payment is Egyptian-source, subject to statutory exemptions and treaty reduction. The applicable treaty rate varies by agreement and may be lower or may allocate exclusive taxing rights in limited cases. Interest on qualifying foreign loans may be subject to specific exemptions or conditions, including requirements relating to lender status, loan registration, use of funds, and the relevant statutory provision. Service fees, technical fees, software payments, guarantee fees, and mixed royalty arrangements require separate characterization; treaty classification and beneficial-ownership analysis are mandatory.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Egyptian transfer-pricing documentation requirements generally apply to controlled transactions. A Local File is commonly triggered where the aggregate value of a related-party transaction category exceeds EGP 8,000,000 in the relevant fiscal year; the exact threshold, transaction aggregation rules, filing format, and submission deadline must be checked against current ETA regulations and guidance. A Master File generally applies to an Egyptian constituent entity of a multinational enterprise group, and country-by-country reporting generally applies to groups meeting the EUR 750,000,000 consolidated-revenue threshold or the corresponding local-currency test. Separate disclosure and documentation obligations may apply below the Local File threshold.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt does not generally operate a standalone United Arab Emirates-style Economic Substance Regulations regime. Nevertheless, commercial substance is relevant under transfer-pricing rules, beneficial-ownership analysis, anti-avoidance principles, treaty interpretation, permanent-establishment analysis, deductibility rules, and the ETA's authority to challenge artificial or non-business arrangements. The LLC should maintain Egyptian people, premises, decision-making, inventory controls, cold-chain operations, commercial risk management, banking activity, customs capability, and records proportionate to its actual wholesale-import function. A conduit entity with no operational capacity may face denial of deductions, treaty benefits, or the asserted tax characterization.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing import sales, maintaining parallel books, understating inventory or gross margins, using false invoices, omitting related-party transactions, or deliberately claiming fictitious deductions or tax credits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Assessment of unpaid tax, late-payment amounts, administrative penalties, and potential criminal prosecution under Egyptian tax legislation. Fraudulent or repeated conduct can result in substantial monetary penalties and imprisonment, with the sanction depending on the offense, amount, intent, and judicial findings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers, authorized signatories, finance officers, and other responsible persons may incur criminal liability where they personally participate in, direct, approve, or knowingly facilitate the violation. Civil exposure may include tax restitution and damages. A general travel ban or veil piercing is not automatic; courts and competent authorities may impose personal precautionary or enforcement measures where statutory conditions are met.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Understating the customs value of frozen beef or seafood, misdescribing goods, splitting invoices, using related-party prices without support, misclassifying tariff codes, or concealing freight, insurance, assists, commissions, or royalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recovery of customs duty, import taxes, VAT, fines, seizure or confiscation of goods, suspension of customs privileges, and possible criminal proceedings under Egyptian customs legislation. Customs reassessment may also affect deductible cost and transfer-pricing positions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible directors, customs representatives, and signatories may face personal criminal or civil exposure for intentional false declarations or customs fraud. Liability is fact-dependent and is not created solely by holding office.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Pricing imported goods from a foreign group entity above arm's length, shifting profit through unsupported management fees or royalties, failing to document comparables, or using customs and tax positions that are materially inconsistent without reconciliation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Primary adjustment of taxable income, denial or limitation of deductions, secondary tax consequences, documentation penalties, interest, and possible audit escalation. A corresponding adjustment is not automatic and may require competent-authority procedures under an applicable treaty.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers may face personal exposure where they knowingly approve fabricated documentation, sham transactions, or deliberate tax evasion. Ordinary transfer-pricing disagreement generally creates corporate tax exposure rather than automatic personal imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to withhold and remit cross-border tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, interest, royalties, technical services, or other potentially Egyptian-source amounts to non-residents without withholding, without verifying treaty residence, or without remitting and reporting the tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Egyptian payer may be assessed for the unwithheld tax, related interest or additions, filing penalties, and penalties for inaccurate withholding returns. Contractual gross-up clauses do not eliminate the payer's statutory obligation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Authorized signatories and responsible finance personnel may incur personal liability for deliberate failure to withhold, false certificates, or misappropriation of withheld tax. Mere corporate non-payment does not automatically pierce the corporate veil.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to register where required, failure to issue compliant tax invoices, claiming unsupported input VAT, omitting domestic sales, or treating imports and local wholesale supplies as outside the VAT system.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Assessment of VAT, denial of input credits, late-filing and late-payment penalties, administrative fines, suspension of tax registration, and criminal exposure for deliberate false invoices or tax fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible managers and signatories may face personal criminal liability for intentional VAT fraud or false documentation; ordinary VAT assessments ordinarily remain liabilities of the LLC.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using opaque beneficial owners, unexplained third-party payments, cash settlement of high-value imports, sanctions-evasive shipping structures, trade-based money laundering, bribery of customs or food-safety officials, or failure to maintain customer and supplier due diligence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Suspicious-transaction reporting, account freezing, transaction rejection, regulatory investigation, confiscation, substantial fines, license consequences, and criminal penalties, including imprisonment, under Egyptian AML, anti-corruption, customs, and criminal laws.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers may be personally prosecuted for participation, authorization, knowledge, facilitation, obstruction, or failure to establish legally required controls. Asset freezing and travel restrictions may arise under applicable judicial or investigative orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company and lack of commercial substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining an Egyptian LLC only as a pass-through for foreign invoices, with no genuine employees, premises, inventory control, commercial decision-making, banking function, or operational responsibility for the cold-chain business.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, recharacterization of transactions, disallowance of deductions, transfer-pricing adjustments, withholding assessments, permanent-establishment assertions, and potential anti-evasion or fraudulent-document proceedings where the structure is sham-based.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil restitution and criminal exposure if they knowingly operate a sham entity or submit false records. A lack of substance alone does not automatically create imprisonment or veil piercing; intent, participation, and statutory breach must be established.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Food, veterinary, import, and cold-chain licensing breach
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Importing frozen meat or seafood without required permits, veterinary or sanitary approvals, traceability records, temperature controls, labeling, storage authorization, or compliant disposal procedures.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Cargo detention, rejection, destruction or re-export, license suspension, administrative fines, product seizure, business closure orders, and possible criminal liability for unsafe, adulterated, or falsely labeled food.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and operational managers may be personally liable where they knowingly place unsafe or unlawfully imported products on the market. Civil claims may include consumer, public-health, and commercial damages.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to retain invoices, customs entries, inventory ledgers, temperature records, transfer-pricing analyses, board approvals, ownership information, or electronic accounting data for the statutory retention period.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Record-keeping fines, adverse tax estimation, denial of deductions and credits, audit penalties, beneficial-owner disclosure consequences, and escalation where missing records conceal tax or AML offenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The LLC and responsible signatories may be liable for statutory record failures. Personal criminal exposure generally requires proof of intentional destruction, falsification, obstruction, or knowing participation in the underlying offense.
